newsitem.title: UK: Aircraft spread deadly viruses, report says.
newsitem.headline: Aircraft spread deadly viruses, report says.

text.p: Aircraft could be spreading dangerous viruses around the world in the sewage from on-board toilets, U.S. researchers reported.

Researchers who took samples the waste pumped from commercial aircraft were horrified to discover that nearly half contained infectious viruses that survived the chemicals in the sewage tanks, New Scientist magazine said on Thursday.

"It was a bit of a jolt for us," the magazine quoted Mark Sobsey, an environmental scientist at the University of North Carolina, as telling a meeting of the American Society for Microbiology in Miami Beach.
Sobsey's group had been asked by the World Health Organisation and the U.S. centres for Disease Control to look for viruses in aircraft heads. They did not find polio, to their relief.
But they did find enteroviruses that cause stomach upset and fever.

"The range of illnesses that can be transmitted by the world's airlines is quite worrisome," Sobsey said. He was concerned hepatitis viruses could be spread in this way, as well as bacteria and parasites.
Sobsey said airline waste in the United States was treated in commercial sewage plants, which do not always kill all types of virus.
"That means one to 10 percent of the viruses survive and are discharged into the environment," he said. "We think there's a risk."
He suggested adding stronger chemicals to all aircraft toilets.
